text: You just started a new game, ready for action. The tutorial pops up: "Press 'A' to jump." Seriously? You've gamed for years, this is so obvious!
Your brain processes movements instantly. To you, it's not learning, just a delay before fun. It just feels frustrating.
Developers don't design just for experts. They build games for *everyone*, from pros to first-time controller users.
Without guidance, new players might struggle, get frustrated, and quit quickly. That's a huge loss for the game.
So, the "obvious" tutorial isn't for you. It's a small investment to onboard everyone, ensuring they grasp basics and stay for the experience.
Next time a game says "Press 'A' to jump," you might still roll your eyes. But now, you'll see the invisible system welcoming *every* player.
